input.brief: Digital design studio for the event industry: animated party posters and video ad creatives, websites and press kits for DJs, logos, brand characters

direction.name: The sentence is the layout
direction.idea: One short sentence, set at poster scale, is the composition. The trick that makes it an idea rather than a big headline: something from the subject sits inside the sentence where a word would be. A strip of photograph fills the gap between two words; a small live fragment of the product replaces the noun; the object the sentence names is pictured at the size of a letter. Write the sentence first, find the word that can be shown instead of said, and put the showing in its place. The reader completes the sentence with their eyes.
direction.composition: The sentence is four to seven words and runs as one or two full-width lines at 9–13vw. Inline with the type, on the baseline, sits one media slot: a rounded-rectangle or square frame exactly one line-height tall and two to three ems wide, holding a photograph or a looping crop. Above and below the sentence the screen is empty except for a small navigation line and one supporting sentence set small, both on the same left margin. Later sections repeat the grammar at smaller scale: each is a short statement on the left six columns with its proof (image, figure, list) on the right, so the page reads as a series of sentences with evidence. Generous vertical space (160px or more) between sections.
direction.typography: Display weight with real presence (medium to bold), tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, leading 0.95–1.0 so two lines sit close. The inline frame aligns to cap height and baseline exactly; set it with em units so it scales with the type.
direction.colour: A calm ground with ink at full contrast. The only colour comes from the photograph inside the sentence; if the palette has an accent, use it once, on the action.
direction.imagery: One strong, simple photograph that reads at small size (a face, an object, a texture, a horizon), cropped to a wide strip inside the sentence. The same image may open to full width in the next section, so the small slot feels like a window onto something larger.
direction.richness: The collision of big type and one live image inside it. Because there is only one image on the first screen, choose it with care and give it perfect alignment to the letters.
direction.pitfalls: The sentence must be short enough for two lines on a phone, where the inline frame drops to its own line between the two halves. Do not style one word differently to fake the device. Do not use more than one slot per sentence.

hero.name: Title in the sky, line on the horizon
hero.blueprint: One wide photograph or render fills the viewport, chosen with the subject in the lower 55% and open sky, fog or a plain wall above it. The headline is centred in that empty upper zone: two lines at clamp(72px, 7.2vw, 112px), leading 0.9, its cap line 72px from the top, the first line short and the second longer so the block widens towards the subject. On the horizon, with its baseline at 52% of the height, one supporting sentence is split into two halves at 22px: the first half right-aligned to end at column 5, the second left-aligned from column 8, so the subject shows through the 260px gap between them. Wordmark top-left on a 32px margin; up to three text links from column 9; the single action top-right as a solid rectangle in the paper colour. All type is in one ink chosen against the sky; on a pale sky use the photograph's darkest tone rather than black. Nothing else crosses the lower half.
hero.mobile: The picture is re-cropped to portrait with the subject in the lower 45%. The headline sits centred in the sky at 11vw on two lines, 96px down, and the two halves of the sentence become two centred lines at 17px directly under it. The action is a full-width button 24px above the bottom edge on a neutral scrim band 96px tall. Wordmark top-left and a menu word top-right.
hero.headline: Two lines, the second the longer, at most about 14 characters per line: the name of the place, or a 3–5 word claim about it.

type.note: One variable family pushed to its narrowest, heaviest setting for headlines and relaxed to normal width for text, so display and body share a skeleton. Suits sportswear, campaigns and fintech pages that speak in capitals.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One frame, three distances
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300vh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. On the stage one frame is centred: 30vw wide at 4:5, square corners, overflow hidden. Inside it the same photograph is shown at three distances as the reader scrolls: the whole subject, then scaled to 180% toward one detail, then to 320% on a second detail (transform: scale with a transform-origin per stage, 700ms ease, switched by IntersectionObserver on three invisible markers). The sentence is delivered in halves: its first two or three words sit above the frame at clamp(56px, 8vw, 130px), centred; the last words arrive below the frame at the second stage, overlapping the frame's bottom edge by 0.3em. At the third stage one caption of 28ch at 17px appears to the right of the frame, top-aligned. The two halves together are the heading and stay within two lines.
sections.mobile: The frame grows to 70vw at 4:5 and stays sticky at centre. The first half of the sentence sits above it at 13vw, the second half below it at the same size. The third-stage caption appears under the sentence at 16px, centred.

sections.name: Names as one paragraph
sections.blueprint: All project or client names run together as one paragraph at poster scale: 10–18 names at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 78px), leading 1.1, flowing inline across the full width between 24px margins and wrapping where they fall, five to seven lines in all. Names are separated by a comma, or by a small inline frame: an `inline-block` 0.8em tall and 1.2em wide, aligned to the cap height, holding that project's photograph and placed directly after its name. Every name is a link; all names rest in the soft ink, and the hovered one takes full ink while its inline frame scales to 1.6 times from its left edge. A heading of two words opens the paragraph as its first words in full ink, on the same line and at the same size, followed by a colon. Below the paragraph at the left margin, one line at 15px gives the count and the years covered.
sections.mobile: The paragraph is set at 9vw, left-aligned, about twelve lines, with names separated by commas. Inline frames are removed except after the first three names, where they stay at cap height. All names are full ink; each remains a link with 6px of extra line spacing for touch.

sections.name: Prints dropped on the headline
sections.blueprint: A flat colour field 100svh tall. A two-line headline of two to four words in an ultra-condensed or ultra-heavy face is centred, each line clamp(120px, 14vw, 210px) tall with leading 0.85. Two portrait photographs, each about 26vw wide at 3:4 with an 8px solid white border like a print, are absolutely placed on top of the headline's centre: one rotated −8 degrees, one +6 degrees, overlapping each other by a third and hiding roughly half the letters, so the eye completes the words. A third, smaller print (16vw) may sit at the lower right, cropped by the section's bottom edge. One plain sentence at 16px sits at the bottom-left margin, 24px from the edges. The prints are above the type in the stacking order; hovering one brings it to the front and straightens it to 0 degrees over 200ms. Nothing else is on the field.
sections.mobile: Headline lines at 30vw, still two lines, centred in a 78svh field. Two prints only, each 52vw wide, rotated −6 and +5 degrees, overlapping at the headline's centre. The small sentence sits at the bottom-left margin at 15px.

sections.name: Statement, table pushed right
sections.blueprint: A heading of four to six words spans the full width on two lines at clamp(40px, 4.5vw, 68px), left-aligned with its first line indented 3vw and leading 0.98. 96px below, the table is pushed into the right-hand five columns (8–12) and the left stays open. One plain word naming the table (offices, hours, rates) hangs at 14px in column 7, top-aligned with the first row. Each row is a three-part line at 15–16px with 26px between rows: the kind or day in the soft ink at the left of the measure, the place or service at 30%, and the address, time or price right-aligned, with a small arrow where the row links. Rows are separated by space only; every fourth row has 44px above it to form groups. In columns 1–4, bottom-aligned with the last row, one 4:5 photograph 22vw wide may sit alone. Holds 5–14 rows.
sections.mobile: Heading at 9.5vw without the indent. The table takes the full width at 16px; each row stacks the kind above the place, with the value right-aligned on the first line. The naming word is dropped because the heading already says it. The photograph follows at 60% width on the right margin.

sections.name: Portrait as drop cap
sections.blueprint: No heading. One biography paragraph of 50–80 words is set large at clamp(24px, 2.5vw, 38px), regular weight, leading 1.2, across columns 3–12 of the grid. A square portrait is floated at the paragraph's start with `float: left`: its side equals three lines of text (3.6em), with 0.5em of space to its right, so the first three lines wrap beside it and the fourth returns to the paragraph's left edge, like a drop capital. Square corners. The person's name, the first words of the paragraph, is in full ink; the rest may be in a softer ink with linked names in full ink and underlined. A second paragraph follows after one blank line in the soft ink at the same size. Columns 1–2 hold three short facts (place, since when, how to reach) at 14px, top-aligned with the portrait. Section padding 140px.
sections.mobile: Text at 22px with leading 1.25, full width. The portrait keeps its float but grows to four lines tall, about 110px square. The three facts move below the second paragraph as a single row of three small blocks at 13px.

sections.name: Names as one sentence
sections.blueprint: Client, press or partner names are written out as one run-on sentence and set large: clamp(40px, 5vw, 76px), leading 1.0, flush left across all twelve columns, wrapping naturally over five to seven lines. Names are separated by commas and the list ends with a full stop. All names are set in a dimmed ink (still at least 3:1 against the ground), so the block reads as texture; one name at a time is lit in the full ink, and the lit name moves through the list every two seconds (a class toggled by a short script, with a 400ms colour transition). The sentence opens with two or three plain words in the full ink that act as the heading: the phrase that introduces the names. Nothing else is in the section: no logos, no columns, and 120px of space above and below.
sections.mobile: The same sentence at 9vw, wrapping over ten to fourteen lines; cut the list to the twelve strongest names so it stays within one and a half screens. The lit name still cycles. Margins are 20px and there are no other elements.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: Spatial
references.idea: Typography behaves like sound in a room: plain black statements swell, stretch and bend through an empty white viewport as you scroll.
references.hero: A white viewport holding only the festival dates: two centred lines in Neue Haas Grotesk Roman at roughly 6.7vw, black, tight leading, sitting at the exact vertical middle and spanning about half the width. Large empty fields above and below; no image, no button, no supporting copy. The header is the only other element: a light uppercase wordmark with tight tracking flush to the top-left corner at a 20px inset, and nine small bold uppercase links in a row across the top right. Mobile is the same poster at 40px with a two-line hamburger.
references.type: One face, Neue Haas Grotesk Display 55 Roman, for everything: statements from 56px up to about 10vw, 13px body, bold 13px uppercase navigation, a timetable at about 16px with tight leading. Statement lines are distorted per glyph, each letter scaled to a different width and height.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e8a25c — Pure black on pure white; the programme section inverts to white on black. The only colour is the amber haze of a single photograph.
references.imagery: Almost none. The images are canvas-rendered text statements warped and magnified until letter fragments become abstract black shapes cropped by the viewport. One warm, hazy venue photograph sits inset at half width beside body copy, square-cornered.
references.layout: Full width with 10 to 20px margins. Opens with one centred statement per screen, then drops into left-aligned two-column copy and, further down, edge-to-edge four-column timetables. The swing between empty poster screens and tightly packed listings is the page's rhythm.

sections.description: A run of full-viewport white screens, each carrying one centred two-line sentence. The text is drawn on canvas and deformed: letters within a word have different widths and heights and baselines wobble. Between screens the type is magnified so far that only the strokes and counters of a few letters cross the frame, cropped on every side, while a small readable version of the next sentence appears inside the wreckage of the previous one.

A calm reset: a three-line centred statement at about 5vw in undistorted type fills the top half. At the bottom, a column of 16px body copy about 650px wide sits flush to the left margin, and an amber-toned photograph starts at the horizontal centre and runs to the right margin with square corners, cropped by the fold.

Black full-bleed section. Day headings are single small lines above a hairline; under each, a four-column table spans the full width: artist flush left, format at one third, room at two thirds, time range right-aligned at the far edge. Rows are about 35px high with a hairline between each, all in the same 30px grotesk with no bold; changeovers are marked by rows in capitals.

steal: Open with a single factual line (the dates) centred on an otherwise empty white screen instead of a branded hero.
Scale each letter of a statement independently in width and height so plain grotesk type looks as if it is resonating.
Set a programme as a full-width four-column hairline table in one size and weight, times right-aligned, on an inverted background.

references.name: Colonia Zacamil
references.idea: The sentence is the layout: 'FLY TO ___ ZACAMIL' runs as one full-width line, with a strip of drone video filling the gap where a word would sit.
references.hero: Warm off-white field with no navigation at all. One line of black ultra-condensed capitals about 13vw tall sits on the vertical centre and runs edge to edge with 28px side margins: 'FLY', a wide gap, 'TO', then a rounded-corner strip of aerial video exactly as tall as the letters and half the viewport wide, then 'ZACAMIL'. A tiny mono bracket label sits above the last word. About 150px lower, a small black pill button with a white dot-in-circle at its right end is centred. Two centred lines of 24px serif sit near the bottom edge. The top third is empty.
references.type: Heathergreen, an ultra-condensed regular-weight sans, in capitals at 187px; Reckless Neue serif at 24px for the caption; Roboto Mono for the button and bracket label. Three faces, each used once, with roughly an 8:1 jump and no tracking adjustments.
references.colour: #ebe6e0 #000000 #3d4633 #8d8a84 #4d8fa3 — Warm putty paper with pure black type and button. The only colour on the page is inside the video strip: tree greens, roof greys and one patch of teal.
references.imagery: Top-down drone footage of housing blocks and trees, cropped to an extreme letterbox near 5:1 with 14px rounded corners and used as a word inside the headline; on mobile it becomes a 2:1 block between two headline lines.
references.layout: Single viewport, no scroll captured. Everything hangs on the central axis: full-width headline line mid-screen, button below, caption at the foot. About 80% of the screen is bare paper. On mobile the sentence stacks into three bands: words, video, word.
steal: Replace a word in the headline with a media strip cut to the cap height, so the picture is read as part of the sentence.
Use three type voices once each (ultra-condensed display, soft serif caption, mono button) instead of one family in many sizes.
On mobile, restack the same sentence as word / image / word at full width rather than shrinking the single line.

references.name: Warm & Fuzzy
references.idea: A showreel-first studio site in which every section takes one flat, loud colour (blue, black, yellow) under heavy grotesk type and a chunky custom wordmark.
references.hero: The showreel plays full-bleed with a visible film-grain overlay and no scrim. A chunky hand-cut wordmark sits top left, 16px from the edges; the same top line continues with a one-sentence status link, a tiny thumbnail beside the latest project's name, and three caps links at the far right, all white over the footage. A small green caps play label floats at dead centre. The tagline is anchored bottom left, 16px from both edges, in white grotesk caps at 47px (3.3vw) on one line spanning 56% of the width. A tiny square pause control sits bottom right.
references.type: SuisseIntl throughout, rendering heavy, tracked -0.027em: a 47px caps tagline, a caps section title at 9.4vw, statement paragraphs around 5vw with tight leading, and 10 to 11px caps captions. The logo is custom chunky lettering with wobbly cut-paper counters.
references.colour: #000000 #190bb6 #f7dd47 #ffffff #e9479f #1fc27a — Each section is a flat field: ultramarine blue, black, yellow, then blue again. White type on blue and black, black on yellow; a green play label is the only small accent.
references.imagery: Commercial stills and video (candy-coloured CG worlds, product renders, live-action frames) in square-cornered thumbnails of mixed aspect ratios, with a grain layer over the whole page and floating glossy 3D sticker objects.
references.layout: Tight 16px outer margins and edge-to-edge type. Sections are told apart by background colour rather than spacing: a blue statement set in the right two-thirds, a black packed work wall, a yellow full-width paragraph, a blue footer.

sections.description: On black, a tiny caps motto sits top left, then a caps section title at about 9vw flush left with a small underlined link at the far right on its baseline. Beneath, thumbnails pack into an uneven wall: widths vary from one-sixth to one-half of the page, heights differ, gaps are about 8px and rows do not align. Under each image a 10px caps line gives the project name left and the year in grey right.

A yellow field filled edge to edge by one paragraph in black heavy grotesk at roughly 5vw with very tight leading, left-aligned at the 16px margin. Several lines contain deliberate word-sized gaps, as if the text flowed around something, and a small tilted image chip floats over the first lines, covering parts of words.

A full-screen blue field. A top row of tiny caps, email left and three links right, sits above a hairline. A glossy 3D sticker object hangs near the top centre. The chunky wordmark runs the full page width at the bottom in white, about a fifth of the viewport tall, above a bar of tiny caps links divided by vertical hairlines.

steal: Give every section one flat saturated background and change it at each section break, keeping type strictly black or white.
Pack work thumbnails at mixed widths and heights with 8px gaps and a two-part micro caption (name left, year right) under each.
End with the wordmark at full page width on a colour field, with all utility links reduced to a tiny caps bar split by vertical hairlines.
references.media: A 6s muted showreel covers the whole first screen with the nav and title on it and no scrim. Below: an asymmetric top-aligned mosaic of three tile widths (5, 7 and 12 of 24 columns) reshuffled each row with captions under, small inline thumbnails between words of a large paragraph, clips cut into geometric clip-path shapes, a full-bleed photo band with a marquee across its lower edge, and a glossy 3D cube drifting over text and the footer, all at 0px radius under a grain layer that steps every second.
references.motion: A brief ultramarine preloader with a tilted card, then the header and title slide and scale in over 0.5s after a 0.75s delay while the reel carries the motion. Lenis with CSS scroll-driven animations reveals blocks on the scroll timeline, parallaxes figures by 5 to 25svh, translates stacked assets in over 0.75s with a per-item delay and slides a giant sentence left with the scroll, all on one house ease, cubic-bezier(.26,1,.48,1), at 0.5s, with 29 reduced-motion rules.
